problem_statement: The sujoyduttajad Landing-Page-React project is a runnable React marketing landing page for ULTRA with a sticky top navigation bar, dark hero and info sections, a three-card pricing grid, a footer, and separate /services, /products, and /sign-up routes. The site advertises integrations with a customer's marketing stack in copy but exposes no dedicated Connectors directory, and the navigation bar has no entry pointing to one. Add a new cross-page Connectors directory that reuses the site's existing card-grid and navigation design system: build a /connectors page from the same dark-section, blue-accent, compact-card visual language as the Pricing grid, register a Connectors entry in the shared navigation registry so the same nav-link renders consistently on the homepage and on the new page, and add a category filter above the connector grid (All / CRM / Ads / Automation) with a live readout of the form Showing N of 6 that updates as the visitor filters. The navigation bar, footer, hero, pricing cards, imagery, typography, responsive behavior, and the existing /services, /products, /sign-up routes must be preserved unchanged.
required_content: Add a new /connectors route and page that renders inside the existing React Router shell (shared Navbar and Footer).
The Connectors page must include the exact heading Connectors and the exact intro Plug ULTRA into the marketing stack.

Add six visible connector cards built from the shared card-grid pattern (icon + h3 title + description), with the exact titles Salesforce CRM Sync, HubSpot Campaign Bridge, Google Ads Import, Meta Lead Ads Intake, Slack Alert Hooks, Zapier Automation.

Add a category filter above the grid with All, CRM, Ads, and Automation tabs and a live readout; selecting a category filters the visible cards and updates the readout (for example, selecting Ads shows the wording Showing 2 of 6).
Include the exact summary text Every ULTRA connector uses the same secure lead pipeline.
Register a Connectors entry in the shared navigation registry so a nav-link labelled Connectors renders on every page (homepage and the Connectors page).
Reuse the existing ULTRA visual system: dark #101522 section, blue #4b59f7 accents, #242424 compact cards with the shared shadow, white headings, muted #a9b3c1 supporting text.
Preserve the existing ULTRA navbar, hero copy, Sarah Jeni testimonial, Instant Setup section, Our Services pricing cards, Secure Database section, footer newsletter, and the local svg/jpg imagery.
Do not add dependencies, remote assets, new route frameworks, generated build output edits, or unrelated pricing/navbar/footer rewrites.
design_constraints: Treat this as a cross-page design-continuity addition: the new directory must look and behave like a native part of the existing ULTRA site, not a detached or off-system page.
Build the Connectors card grid from the same styled-components card pattern used by the Pricing grid (icon, h3 title, description) so the visual identity matches.
Register the new section once in a shared navigation registry and render it through the existing Navbar so the nav-link appears consistently across pages.
The category filter must derive its readout and its visible cards live from the selected category; the readout must reflect the current selection rather than a value captured once at page load.
The six cards must form a three-column desktop grid, the filter tabs must wrap, and everything must stack cleanly on tablet and mobile without horizontal overflow or overlapping cards.
Keep the existing route pages unchanged and reachable at /services, /products, and /sign-up.
Keep the change scoped to a new Connectors page folder plus the shared navigation registry and the router; do not modify package.json, lockfiles, image files, or generated build artifacts.
state_constraints: desktop_home, mobile_home, and tablet_home verify the shared Navbar renders the registered Connectors nav-link cross-page and the original hero, pricing cards, imagery, and footer remain intact.

desktop_connectors, mobile_connectors, and tablet_connectors verify the new Connectors page renders the shared card grid (heading, six card titles, summary), the category filter tab row, and the same registered nav-link, and remains responsive without horizontal overflow.

desktop_connectors_ads verifies that clicking the Ads category tab updates the live readout to Showing 2 of 6 and narrows the grid to the Ads connectors, rather than leaving a readout that was captured at page load.
All states verify the original React Router shell, navbar, footer, and local media assets continue to render with zero console or network errors under the CRA production build harness.

change_completion: The Connectors page renders the exact heading, intro, six card titles, and summary text.
A Connectors nav-link is registered in the shared navigation registry and renders on both the homepage and the Connectors page.
The category filter updates its live readout and the visible cards when a category tab is selected (selecting Ads yields Showing 2 of 6).
design_consistency: The Connectors cards reuse the existing dark-section, blue-accent, compact-card visual language of the Pricing grid.
The new directory reads as a native part of the ULTRA site rather than an off-system standalone page, with a tidy filter tab row and a non-overlapping card grid.
The existing hero, testimonial, onboarding, pricing, secure-database, navbar, and footer sections retain their visual identity.
responsive: The six cards form a three-column desktop grid and stack cleanly on 390px mobile without clipping, overlap, or horizontal overflow.
The category filter tab row wraps and stays readable at mobile, tablet, and desktop widths.
The existing route pages remain usable on desktop and mobile.
regression: The CRA app still builds and serves through the benchmark harness with the legacy OpenSSL runtime compatibility used by SiteContinuum.
No dependency, generated build output, image replacement, navbar rewrite, pricing rewrite, or route removal is introduced.
The original /services, /products, and /sign-up pages still expose their expected text and local imagery.

author_notes: Product-grade Consistency (design_continuity / add / cross_page) task on a healthy CRA React Router marketing repo (sujoyduttajad Landing-Page-React, styled-components ULTRA visual system, local svg/jpg imagery). The reference adds a shared navigation registry, a Connectors integration directory built from the existing card-grid design system with a native category filter (All/CRM/Ads/Automation) that derives a live Showing N of 6 readout, and a /connectors route; the Connectors nav-link then renders consistently across the homepage and the new page. Baseline registers the same correct filter wiring but ships a broken fixed-width no-wrap filter rail that runs off-canvas on desktop and overflows the mobile viewport, and it omits the Connectors nav registration. The bad solution snapshots the readout and the shown cards at page load so clicking a category highlights the tab but never updates the readout or the grid, collapses the card grid into an overlapping shingled row, and also omits the nav registration. Acceptance is enforced with four orthogonal product-grade gates: no_horizontal_overflow (mobile filter rail), visual_regression (filter+grid crops), dom_assertions (cross-page nav-link + filter tabs), and interaction_assertions (the Ads filter readout), plus enforce_console_errors (max 0).
